title: Maximum Product Subarray
corePattern: Dynamic Programming with Dual State Tracking (Modified Kadane for Product)
interviewTips: Clarify constraints: can array contain zeros and negatives? Is n up to 2*10^4 and product fits in 32-bit int? Ask if empty subarray allowed (here no, at least one element).
Trade-off to discuss: Brute force O(n^2) is simple but fails on large n; DP O(n) time O(1) space is optimal because sign flips require tracking both max and min ending at i.
Edge-case tip: mention single element, all negatives with odd count, zeros splitting array, and single negative like [-2] where answer is -2, not 0.

approaches.name: Approach 1: Brute Force
approaches.intuition: Enumerate every subarray starting at i and extend to j, maintain running product, and keep the global maximum. This directly implements the definition of maximum product subarray.
approaches.theory: For each start index i, iterate end index j >= i and maintain prod = product(nums[i..j]). Update ans = max(ans, prod). There are n*(n+1)/2 subarrays, each extension is O(1) multiplication. Correct because all possibilities are examined. Space is O(1) besides input.

timeComplexity.explanation: n start positions each expands up to n ends, total O(n^2) multiplications and comparisons.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Only prod and ans variables, no extra array.

edgeCases: Overflow not an issue per constraints but product grows fast in brute force

approaches.name: Approach 2: DP Tracking Max and Min (Optimal)
approaches.intuition: Product differs from sum because a negative times a very small (negative) value becomes very large. So at each position we must remember both the largest and smallest product of a subarray ending here. A negative flips them.
approaches.theory: Let maxEnd[i] = max product of subarray ending at i, minEnd[i] = min product ending at i. Recurrence: if nums[i] >= 0 then maxEnd[i]=max(nums[i], maxEnd[i-1]*nums[i]), minEnd[i]=min(nums[i], minEnd[i-1]*nums[i]); if nums[i] < 0 they swap roles. This is because any optimal subarray ending at i either starts at i or extends optimal previous subarray. Only previous max/min needed, so compress to O(1) space with curMax, curMin. Global ans = max over maxEnd[i].

timeComplexity.explanation: Single left-to-right pass, O(1) work per element.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Only curMax, curMin, ans variables; no DP array needed.

steps: x=-2: swap -> curMax=3 curMin=6, curMax=max(-2,-6)=-2 curMin=min(-2,-12)=-12 ans=6

edgeCases: [-2,0,-1] -> 0: zero resets, curMax/curMin restart via max(x, ...)
[-2] -> -2: loop not entered, ans is nums[0]
[-2,3,-4] -> 24: two negatives make positive, requires min tracking
[0,2] -> 2 and [2,0] -> 2: zero does not force answer to 0
